To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fault-related and the shear zone-related granitic intrusions are mainly generated by crustal partial melting, and they crystallize in the upper crust, within or above the shear zones, during or after the deformation of their host rocks.

granitoid intrusives of the Central Sudete and of the Middle- Odra Fault Zone are both spatially (i.e. they are intruded within shear zones and along faults) and temporally related (i.e. their emplacement is synchronous with tectonic movements in the shear zones) to the final stages in the tectonothermal evolution of the shear zones.

the granitoid intrusives of the Central Sudetan and the MOFZ areas, which are both spatially associated with large-scale shear zones, are related to the final tectono-metamorphic stages of the evolution of these shear zones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new type of granitoids that are genetically related to large-scale crustal shear zones and faults.
the temporal and spatial relationship between magmatism and tectonothermal events in a collisional setting, and the influence of tectonic structures on the emplacement of magmas.
the temporal relationships between the emplacement of the granitoids and the activity of the shear zone.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the granitoids are genetically related to the shear zones and faults.
the granitoid intrusives in the Bohemian massif are related to the final stage of tectonics, and are not a product of the Variscan orogeny.
the emplacement of the granitoids was related to the late, final stages of tetrane amalgamation and crustal thickening, and was accompanied by a significant increase in the thermal gradients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the granitoid emplacement was coeval with ductile, trans-current movements along the shear zone.
the granitoids of these shear zones were formed during the final stages of the Variscan orogeny and that their emplacement was coeval with transcurrent movements along shear zones.
the granitoid intrusives of the CS and of the MOFZ represent the products of partial melting of the crustal rocks, and that they were emplaced within the shear zones at a depth of c. 20  km.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the granitoids are not only genetically related to the shear zones and faults, but are also good markers for the tectonometamorphic evolution of the shear zone.

the emplacement of the granitoid intrusives was not a result of tectonic overpressure but rather a consequence of a local increase in thermal gradient, which is related to the ductile transcurrent movements along shear zones.
the granitoid intrusives related to shear zones may be used as markers of their tectonic evolution, and the shear zones may serve as a guide to the search for granitoids in the crust.
